message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles typically covers about 380–400 miles (roughly 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—no major construction or heavy traffic—a straight drive at an average speed of around 60 mph would take roughly **6 to 7 hours**.

Keep in mind:

- **Traffic:** Peak times (morning/evening rush hour, weekends, holidays) can add 30–90 minutes or more, especially near the Bay Area and the Los Angeles metro area.
- **Stops:** If you plan to stop for meals, refueling, or sightseeing (e.g., stops in Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo), add extra time accordingly.
- **Roadwork/Incidents:** Check real‑time traffic updates (Google Maps, Waze, or local news) before you depart; unexpected delays can push the trip closer to 8–9 hours.

So, expect a minimum of about 6 hours under ideal conditions, but plan for up to 8–9 hours if you’re traveling during busy periods or want to make scenic stops along the way.
